title: Paramedic officer
description: Review (medicines, IV, intubation) + breathing patterns, CPR medicines and procedures, ECG rhythms: shockable or not.

questions.q: Wheezing, the patient can only speak in short words. What do you think of?
Crackles, swollen ankles, pink frothy sputum. What is it and what is the treatment?
answers: Pulmonary oedema: sit up, Nitroglycerin, oxygen

questions.q: Deep, fast breathing with an acetone smell on the breath?
Slow, shallow breathing. What does it point to?
Snoring breathing in an unconscious patient?
answers: Partial airway obstruction: the airway must be secured

questions.q: What does gasping (agonal) breathing mean?
answers: A sign of cardiac arrest: start CPR

questions.q: COPD patient, pursed lips, sitting leaning forward. What helps the most?
Which rhythm is this, and is it shockable?
Which rhythms are shockable?
What do you do in asystole?
answers: CPR and Adrenaline as soon as possible, no shock

questions.q: What is PEA?
answers: Electrical activity without a pulse: CPR, Adrenaline, look for the cause

questions.q: In a shockable rhythm, when do you give the first Adrenaline?
What becomes of untreated ventricular fibrillation within a few minutes?
answers: It turns into asystole, the chance of survival keeps falling
It returns to sinus rhythm by itself

questions.q: Why do we not shock a normal sinus rhythm?
answers: The shock can stop the heart

questions.q: VT with a pulse, unstable patient. What do you do?
Which belong to the “4H” reversible causes of cardiac arrest?
Besides good quality CPR, what improves the chance of ROSC?
How often do the people doing compressions swap?
answers: About every 2 minutes, at the rhythm check

questions.q: What do you do after ROSC?
answers: Monitor, oxygen, watch the blood pressure and the rhythm, transport: it can stop again

questions.q: This rhythm is shown and the patient has no pulse. Is it shockable?
answers: No, it is a normal rhythm

questions.q: This rhythm is shown, the patient does not respond and has no palpable pulse. What do you do?
answers: Pulseless VT: shockable, defibrillation and CPR

questions.q: This rhythm is on the monitor, but there is no palpable pulse on the large arteries. What is it?
answers: PEA: not shockable, CPR and Adrenaline

questions.q: The patient talks, has a palpable pulse, and the monitor shows this. What do you do with the defibrillator?
A patient collapsed suddenly and this rhythm is shown. What matters most?
answers: Defibrillation as soon as possible, CPR in between
Wait, it may settle by itself

questions.q: Which rhythm is NOT shockable?
What do you do after a shock?
answers: Continue CPR at once for 2 minutes, only then check the rhythm
Wait for the pulse to come back

questions.q: Cardiac arrest caused by hypoglycaemia. What do you give besides CPR?
